caption:
You can ask a podcast a question after it's over — and it actually answers.

Most of us have a mental drawer of half-remembered podcast moments: the line about compound interest, the book recommendation from that one guest, the framework the host explained twice because it was that good. And most of us never find it again, because rewinding 40 minutes of audio to locate 12 seconds of insight is not something anyone actually does.

Snipd is an AI podcast player (iOS and Android) built around the idea that listening shouldn't mean losing information. A few things stood out in the research:

→ Triple-tap your headphones mid-episode and it saves the clip, transcript, and an AI summary automatically — no notes app, no pausing, no "I'll remember this later."
→ Chat with Episode lets you ask a question about something the host said after you've finished listening, and it pulls the answer straight from the transcript.
→ AI-generated chapters let you jump straight to the part of a 90-minute episode you actually care about.
→ Guest Detection surfaces who's talking automatically, so you're not pausing to Google a name.
→ Everything exports into Notion, Obsidian, Readwise, or Markdown, so it lands in whatever system you already use instead of dying in the app.

One honest catch: it's built for English-language, podcast/audio-first content, so multilingual listeners may hit rougher edges. It's also a companion layer on top of how you already listen, not a full replacement for your main podcast app.

It's not a concept app either — it's on the App Store and Google Play with a real user base (100K+ downloads, 1.9K reviews), and reviewers describe it as the direct successor to Airr after that app shut down.

Save this so you don't lose it, and give it a real listen on your next commute. Full breakdown — link in bio.

slides.heading: You can ask a podcast a question after it ends
slides.body: Not a metaphor — an actual answer, pulled from the transcript, about something the host said an hour ago.

slides.heading: You've done this: rewind, rewind, still missed it
slides.body: Something great gets said mid-episode and by the time you find a pen, it's gone — or you rewind three times chasing one sentence.

slides.heading: Triple-tap your headphones. That's the whole move.
slides.body: It saves the clip, the transcript, and an AI summary in real time — no pausing, no notes app, no "I'll remember it later."

slides.heading: Ask the episode a direct question later
slides.body: "Chat with Episode" lets you type a question about the conversation and get an answer sourced from what was actually said.

slides.heading: Skip straight to the part you actually care about
slides.body: AI-generated chapters break each episode into topics, so a 90-minute conversation stops being one giant undifferentiated block.

slides.heading: It tells you who's talking, automatically
slides.body: Guest Detection surfaces info on who's on the episode as you listen, so you're not stopping to search a name mid-walk.

slides.heading: Where it falls short
slides.body: It's built for English-language audio and works best as an add-on to your existing podcast app, not a full replacement for it.

slides.heading: Before: a drawer of half-remembered quotes. After: a searchable library.
slides.body: Every highlight, transcript, and summary exports straight into Notion, Obsidian, or Readwise — sitting in your notes instead of your memory.

slides.heading: Save this, then try it on your next commute
slides.body: Download Snipd, triple-tap your headphones once, and see what you've been losing every time you listen.
